shipReasons: No critical defect: every one of the five chapters starts from the new chapter select with real keyboard, real mouse and real touch, reaches party-prep, and returns to the board on Escape; no crash, lock or lost progress was seen in any run.

No regression against the live build fd0ae96: the live site still serves the old `.ig-title-screen` title and a chapter board with no `.fe-card` elements, so every element this review found fault with exists only in the candidate. Nothing that works live is broken here.

The one major finding (FE-001, front-end text below the 14 px legibility floor at 390x844) sits entirely inside the brand-new front end, which does not exist on the live build — a new-feature defect under RUBRIC section 3, disclosed and carried rather than held.

The shared-system half of the change is clean where it matters most: 262 `/art/` requests across all five chapters returned zero 4xx and zero HTML-for-asset responses, no image failed to decode, no monogram fallback was visible in any staged battle, and 363 shipped PNGs scanned zero all-black and zero undecodable.

changedArea is FAIL and ship is SHIP on purpose (RUBRIC section 3): the phone legibility failure keeps the changed area from being accepted, and the candidate is still plainly better than what is live.

issues.title: At phone width the whole new front end sits under the 14 px legibility floor
issues.expected: CHK-003: zero text elements below 14 effective css px on any screen, at every supported viewport including 390x844.
issues.observed: At 390x844 the title has 8 elements under 14 px (eyebrow "An unofficial fan tribute" 9.5 px, the PRESS ENTER chip 11.0 px, all four hint-rail labels 9.5 px) and the chapter select has 43 (eyebrow 11.0, "Chapter I" 10.3, the CTB badge 9.5, both group headings 9.5, every card numeral 9.5, every card name 13.9). Nothing is clipped and the page does not scroll sideways, so the composition survives; it is simply too small to read on a phone. At 1600x900 and 2000x1012 the same screens are clean (minimum 14.4 px and 16.2 px).
issues.repro: Build dist-gate at 8f48237, vite preview, fresh Chromium context at 390x844, load the base, wait for __pyreflyReady, walk every visible text node under `#ui > [data-screen]` taking getComputedStyle fontSize times every ancestor transform scale. Press Enter and repeat on the chapter select.
issues.requirement: critic/CHECKS.md CHK-003; RUBRIC section 2 platform goals (phone is a supported device).
issues.where: src/app/screens/frontend/frontend.css — the front-end type tokens are fixed px rather than clamped against the viewport the way the Ink & Gold tokens are elsewhere.
issues.fix: Floor the front-end type scale the way the pause tokens are floored: give every `.fe-*` size a clamp() whose lower bound is 14 px, and let the phone layout drop cards from the rail rather than shrink their labels.
issues.acceptanceCheck: Re-run the same walk at 390x844 on both screens and see zero elements under 14 px with nothing clipped and no horizontal page scroll.

issues.title: The title's only way forward is a chip that tells a phone player to press Enter
issues.expected: A touch player is told what to do in their own input's words, and a tap on the title advances.
issues.observed: With hasTouch enabled, a tap anywhere on the title plate does nothing; only a tap on the chip advances, and the chip reads "PRESS ENTER". The same is true of the mouse: a click on the background is inert. Once the chip is hit the board is reached normally.
issues.repro: Fresh context with hasTouch, load the base, tap (800, 450) — screen stays 'title'; tap the `.fe-title__chip` box — screen becomes 'chapter-select'.
issues.requirement: RUBRIC section 2 platform goals (touch is a supported control); ControlsHint already words itself per input on the chapter select.
issues.where: src/app/screens/frontend/titleMarkup.ts — the chip's label is a constant, and the plate has no pointer handler.
issues.fix: Give the chip the same per-input wording ControlsHint already does on the board ("Tap to begin" on touch), and make the whole plate the target rather than only the chip.
issues.acceptanceCheck: On a touch context, a tap anywhere on the title reaches chapter-select and the chip's text names a tap.

issues.title: The title figures are larger and further right than the approved frame
issues.expected: The two ink figures sit where docs/concepts/polish/showpiece-frontend/after.png puts them, near the centre of the shore at the scale the target shows.
issues.observed: In the composite the build's pair is appreciably bigger and sits further toward the right edge, close under the headland, rather than centred on the open shore. Every other element of the frame lands on the target. Not covered by any of the deviations the handoff writes down.
issues.repro: node tools/end-state-board.mjs --pair docs/concepts/polish/showpiece-frontend/after.png <title-1600x900.png> and read the composite.
issues.confidence: medium — judged from the composite at 1600x900; the figures' placement is responsive and may read differently at other shapes.
issues.where: src/app/screens/frontend/titleMarkup.ts / frontend.css, the figure height and the shore anchor.
issues.fix: Measure the figure height and x anchor off after.png and restate the two CSS values; no new decision is needed, this is correcting the build to an existing approval.
issues.acceptanceCheck: A fresh composite at 1600x900 in which the pair's scale and x position read as the target's.

issues.title: FFX-2 party chips cut the top of the head
issues.expected: CHK-012: the visible crop contains the whole head, with air above the hair and below the chin.
issues.observed: Paine's and Yuna's battle-start party chips are cropped through the top of the hair — the face is complete, centred and recognisable, and Paine's is clearly her rather than a fallback, but there is no air above the head. Rikku's chip is the loosest of the three and reads correctly.
issues.repro: Stage chapter 4, let the battle-start card settle, zoom the party strip at the foot of the frame.
issues.confidence: medium — the crop boxes for both Paine idles were re-measured in this candidate, so this may be the new measurement or may predate it; the live build's chips were not sampled.
issues.where: src/ui/common/face-crops.json, the Paine and Yuna rows.
issues.fix: Raise the top of those crop boxes by roughly one tenth of the plate height so the hairline clears the chip.
issues.acceptanceCheck: The zoomed party strip in both FFX-2 chapters shows visible background above every head.

issues.title: A click on a COMING card is silently ignored
issues.expected: A player who clicks a locked card learns why nothing happened.
issues.observed: Clicking a COMING card correctly starts nothing and correctly leaves the selection where it was — the guard works. But nothing at all responds, and the next Enter then starts whatever card was already selected, which can read as the locked card having started the wrong chapter.
issues.repro: On the board, click the "Seymour and Anima — Coming" card (selectedId stays seymour-flux), then press Enter (chapter 1 starts).
issues.fix: Play the existing cancel cue and flash the card's COMING badge on a click at a locked tile.
issues.acceptanceCheck: A click on a COMING card produces a visible or audible refusal and still starts nothing.
